depth_justification: It does engage RxBuddy specifics (cloud OCR thumbnails, pharmacy adherence summaries, elderly accessibility, multilingual prescriptions), but is undermined by verbatim looping (Q20=Q25, Q22=Q27, Q23=Q29) and repeatedly wrong citations (EU AI Act 'Article 57' for transparency/oversight/accessibility; GDPR Art. 30 for encryption; Art. 22 for autonomy) plus drifting, reused dimension IDs.
actionability_justification: Mitigations are a mix of concrete recipes (TLS 1.3 + AES-256, SCCs/DPAs, two-step LLM+pharmacist validation, layered consent screen) and directional filler ('conduct audits', 'ensure compliance'), and the final severity-grouped report restates risks but pairs each with only a one-line generic fix.
salient_examples: Reflection Question 20: [P1.D5] Data Minimization in Third-Party Sharing ... (identical to Q25 [P1.D6])
The EU AI Act (Article 57) ... require algorithmic transparency and explainability
Use end-to-end encryption (E2EE) for data in transit (e.g., TLS 1.3) and at rest (e.g., AES-256)
